method: sum of gzip -9 over each module in the route's rel="modulepreload" list, per file, never concatenated
tolerance_basis: 4 builds of identical source, route /, 2026-08-25, this repo: 49193 / 49198 / 49198 / 49205. Range 12 B, and the cause is named - SvelteKit stamps a version string into the entry chunk. 64 B is 5.3x that range; four samples underestimate a true range, so the multiple is the margin. Derived, not measured. If a build ever fails inside 64 B, re-derive it from more builds and more routes rather than nudging it.

/.why: Up for the lens chip on an item's eyebrow. LensChips.svelte plus the six display names in src/lib/payload/lenses.ts reach every route that renders an item. Measured 2026-08-30 on this tree, one session, one node: / 52,584 -> 52,891 (+307), /<date>/ 51,817 -> 52,127 (+310), /<date>/<topic>/ 51,908 -> 52,221 (+313), /archive/ 53,218 -> 53,525 (+307). The control is in the same run and needs no second build: /404, /console/ and /evals/ render no item and all three read inside the 64 B tolerance against their committed records, so this machine agrees with the record on every untouched route and the delta is the change rather than the toolchain. The names are held in a module rather than passed through `data` because `data` repeats all six inside every prerendered day page, and a day page is the heaviest thing we publish - /<date>/ is 350,597 gzipped bytes of HTML against 52,127 of first-load JavaScript. Confirm against the CI site job before trusting the absolute figures: a local Windows build has read 81 to 87 B under CI on every route before now.

/404.why: Runtime and app shell and nothing route-specific. This is the floor every other route sits on. It fell 105 B in the same chunk re-cut that raised /: one module left this route's preload list. Control on this tree: 40,858 B. Every route pays a few tens of bytes for the chart engine existing, without carrying any of it. Measured 2026-08-29 on one machine in one session, origin/main built first and this branch second: / 49,715 -> 49,738, /404 40,769 -> 40,802, /<date>/ 49,591 -> 49,610, /<date>/<topic>/ 49,684 -> 49,702, /archive/ 51,114 -> 51,137, /evals/ 41,725 -> 41,754. On the CI runner, a newer node, the same difference reads 72 to 77 B, which is what pushed /404 2 B past the 64 B tolerance and is why these records moved at all. The module count is unchanged on every route - /404 carries the same 14 modules before and after - so this is not chart code reaching a reading page. It is the shared entry chunk: adding a lazily-imported chunk grows the client manifest the entry embeds, and every route preloads the entry. That is the price of the engine being lazy rather than eager, and it is the right side of the trade: the alternative puts 153,204 B on the console first load instead of 30 B on each page. Up for the icon set. Fifteen glyphs, 2,128 B of marks, reach every route as one generated module because a component names an icon by id and the lookup cannot be tree-shaken on a dynamic key. Measured 2026-08-29 on this tree: / +1,897, /404 +1,771, /<date>/ +1,900, /<date>/<topic>/ +1,900, /archive/ +1,833, /console/ +1,404, /evals/ +1,775. The alternative measured against it was an inline sprite referenced by <use>, which costs no JavaScript at all but puts about 700 B of gzipped markup into every prerendered document - and /404 had 37 B of headroom under its ceiling, so that arm would have had to raise the one ceiling whose whole purpose is keeping the error page tiny. The bytes go where there is room for them. Up for installability. The shell gained a manifest link, an apple-touch-icon link and two media-scoped theme-color tags, plus the code that writes one unconditional theme-color from the resolved background - measured 2026-08-29, 126 to 131 B of first-load JS on every route and 271 B of gzipped markup in every prerendered document. Both are shell costs and neither is avoidable per page: app.html is shared. The apple-touch link in particular cannot be dropped, because Safari probes the ORIGIN root for that filename and this site is served from a project path. DOWN 127 to 150 B, and one module lighter, for the chart vocabulary landing on the console. Measured 2026-08-29: / 51,762 -> 51,613, /404 42,703 -> 42,576, /<date>/ 51,637 -> 51,487, /<date>/<topic>/ 51,728 -> 51,580, /archive/ 53,097 -> 52,961, /evals/ 43,658 -> 43,530, each losing a module from its preload list. The cause is chunking rather than deletion: with five more console-only chart modules in the graph, the bundler stopped hoisting the Chart component into the shared chunk and put it in the console chunk where its only callers now are. The ratchet is two-sided on purpose, so a route getting lighter is recorded rather than left as slack for the next regression to land inside. Up 72 to 149 B for the Panel and StatusChip components entering the shared graph. Measured 2026-08-29: / +72, /404 +149, /<date>/ +72, /<date>/<topic>/ +73, /archive/ +134, /evals/ +145. Only the console draws them, but they are small enough that the bundler keeps them in the shared chunk rather than splitting a chunk for two components. Re-derived 2026-08-29 at the close of the design-system reset, from FIVE builds of identical source taking the HEAVIEST per route rather than the mean - a mean fires on half of all builds. The spread over those five was 13 to 15 B per route, against a 64 B tolerance. This is the first record in this file derived after every sibling row merged rather than while one was still in flight, which is the mistake that set a ceiling from a stacked branch on 2026-08-27 and had it fire 3 days early. Up for the console window control. Every route carries 105 to 111 B of it without rendering any of it: the control is one more client module, and SvelteKit embeds the client manifest in the entry chunk that every route preloads. The module count is unchanged on every route, so this is the manifest and not chart code reaching a reading page. Measured 2026-08-29 on the CI runner, node 22, run 33262132249, against the records this change started from: / 52,474 -> 52,584, /404 42,736 -> 42,841, /<date>/ 51,707 -> 51,817, /<date>/<topic>/ 51,801 -> 51,908, /archive/ 53,109 -> 53,218, /console/ 76,716 -> 78,479, /evals/ 43,687 -> 43,798. Recorded from CI rather than from a developer machine on purpose: the same change measured on node 24.12.0 read 176 B a route instead of 108, and origin/main itself read 81 to 87 B under every committed record there, so a local number is not the number this gate compares against.

/console/.why: Runtime and shell plus the console route: hand-written SVG charts and the d3-scale and d3-array arithmetic behind them, the stage-timing decade axis with its minor stubs and its gap-instead-of-plunge run splitting, the compression scatter that places its articles in the browser, the Charts table that says what the router cost and what it published on each day, and the What the model did table. Up 1,854 B, which is 2.7 percent of the route, for the chart engine arriving: the Chart component, the flow option builder and the token-to-sentinel bridge. About 40 B of that is the toolchain rather than the change - every unrelated route on this machine and this node read 36 to 63 B above its record in the same build, so the change itself is close to 1,810 B. The engine is NOT in this number. It is a lazy chunk of 197,561 B gzipped (585,481 B raw) measured 2026-08-30, fetched only when a chart hydrates, and no page anywhere preloads it - frontend/tests/charts.spec.ts fails the build if one ever does. Registering only the chart types in use is what keeps that number affordable: importing the same package whole read 345,959 B gzipped (1,044,275 B raw) for the same one chart, so the registration list in src/lib/charts/core.ts is worth 56 percent of the download. The console gains a flow diagram over reached, asked, drafted and published, drawn to SVG in Node at build time, so it is on the page with no JavaScript at all and follows a theme change because its colours leave as custom-property references rather than hexes. The prerendered console document is 150,060 B gzip -9 over the committed ledger, against a ceiling of 301,580, leaving 151,520 spare. Up for the icon set. Both are shell costs and neither is avoidable per page: app.html is shared. The apple-touch link in particular cannot be dropped, because Safari probes the ORIGIN root for that filename and this site is served from a project path. Up 3,148 B for the chart vocabulary: a donut gauge, a target bar, a waterfall, stacked bars, a sparkline and the KPI card that carries one. Measured 2026-08-29. Six shapes because there are six questions - one shape repeated six times is what made this page read as a single grey instrument. The arithmetic behind each is a pure function tested without a browser (frontend/tests/vocabulary.spec.ts recomputes every geometry independently); the drawing belongs to the engine and is not ours to test. The engine chunk itself is unchanged in kind - still lazy, still console-only - though it now registers the bar, line and pie types plus the grid, legend and mark-line components those shapes need. Up 544 B for the console frame: panels with an edge and a shadow instead of headings on bare background, sticky table headers, status chips, and a run strip whose day column is derived from the room it has rather than fixed at 16px. Measured 2026-08-29. The strip only ever grows: it clamps at 16 below and 34 above, so a phone keeps the exact behaviour it had - the strip scrolls there and opens on the newest run, which is a behaviour and not a side effect of the cell happening to be 16. Up 616 B, 0.8 percent of the route, for the stage funnel becoming a left-to-right flow diagram: three more nodes, three named loss branches, and the two guards that refuse to draw a flow the counts do not support. Measured 2026-08-30 on one Windows dev machine, node 24, after merging origin/main, with main's own source built on this same tree first and this branch second, two builds each: /console/ 76,727 -> 77,343. Every other route read 0 to 3 B off its record in both arms, so almost none of this is the toolchain. The engine is still not in this number: the lazy chunk went 191,889 -> 197,561 gzipped, 5,672 B for the Sankey layout, and both arms read byte-identical on every build. The 153,204 B it replaces was measured on 2026-08-29 when only the funnel, the tooltip and the SVG renderer were registered - the six-shape vocabulary brought bar, line, pie, grid, legend and mark-line after that and nobody re-measured, so the record sat 25 percent under the truth. The prerendered console document is 163,089 B gzip -9, heaviest of two builds, against a ceiling of 301,580, leaving 138,491 spare - up 864 B on main's own heaviest, which is 0.29 percent of the ceiling. Re-derived 2026-08-29 at the close of the design-system reset, from FIVE builds of identical source taking the HEAVIEST per route rather than the mean - a mean fires on half of all builds. The spread over those five was 13 to 15 B per route, against a 64 B tolerance. This is the first record in this file derived after every sibling row merged rather than while one was still in flight, which is the mistake that set a ceiling from a stacked branch on 2026-08-27 and had it fire 3 days early. Re-measured on the CI runner 2026-08-30 after merging main's ranked console primitives: /console/ reads 79,230 B against main's own record of 78,571, so the flow diagram costs 659 B on that tree rather than the 616 measured before the merge. Every other route read 5 to 9 B above its own record in the same CI build, so a few of those bytes are the runner and not this change. The prerendered console document reads 164,246 B there against the 301,580 ceiling, leaving 137,334 spare. Up for being able to read a date off the stage-timing chart. That chart printed one string for its whole span and drew no mark at any point, so a spike could not be attributed to a day and there was nothing for a pointer or an arrow key to land on. The route grew 608 B against the record, measured 2026-08-30 on an i7-1265U, 12 logical cores, 32 GB, node 24 against a record taken on node 22; every unrelated route read 24 to 37 B BELOW its own record in the same build, so the change itself is close to 640 B, which is 0.8 percent of the route. It buys four functions in src/lib/charts/frame.ts - the thinned day axis, the column x, the readout width cap and the announcement rows - plus a mark at every plotted point, a vertical guide on the hovered column, and the readout strip that took the legend's place rather than joining it. No new dependency and no new chunk: pointerReadout was already on this route for the compression scatter and the throughput candle, so this is the third caller of code already paid for. Up 740 B, 0.93 percent of the route, for the stage-timing chart gaining a date under every column the density allows, a mark at every point, and the strip that reads them: dayTicks, dayColumnX, readoutMarks and readoutCapStyle in src/lib/charts/frame.ts, the pointerReadout action beside observeWidth, and the chart drawing the page's shared time window rather than a calendar built from its own rows. Measured 2026-08-30 on one machine in one session - Windows 11, node v24.12.0, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U - origin/main built first and this branch second: 79,230 -> 79,970. The spread is the six untouched routes in the same build, which read 6 to 10 B above their own records and all inside the 64 B tolerance, so about 8 B of the 740 is the toolchain and the rest is the change. None of it is chart-engine code: the axis, the marks and the strip are plain SVG and one Svelte action, so the lazy chunk is untouched. Up a further 710 B, 0.9 percent of the route, for the throughput trend taking that same contract, so the two charts stacked on the page cannot behave differently: a date under every column through the same dayTicks, a column guide, the readout strip built from readoutMarks and bounded by readoutCapStyle, a dashed rule on every day the model changed, and one line of type where the window holds nothing, so the chart no longer disappears while the timing chart above it explains itself. Measured 2026-08-30 on one machine in one session - Windows 11, node v24.12.0, 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1265U: 79,970 -> 80,680. The spread is the six untouched routes in the same build, which read 17 to 21 B above their own records and all inside the 64 B tolerance, so about 19 B of the 710 is the toolchain and the rest is the change. It consumes frame.ts rather than adding to it, so no new module reaches the first-load path and the lazy chunk is untouched again. Up 1,539 B for the eleven measure cards that replace the What the model did table as the section's leading shape: the per-column series, the window filter, the swap-rule placement and the Sparkline component the cards draw with. That is 1.9 percent of the route, and it buys the one question the table could not answer - did a measure get worse - because a trend is a vertical scan and every column beside the one being scanned was a different quantity. Measured 2026-08-30 on one machine in one session, node v24.12.0 on Windows 11, HEAD built first and this branch second: /console/ 80,671 -> 82,210. The spread is the six untouched routes in the same pair of builds, which read +5 to +7 B, so about 7 B of the 1,539 is the toolchain and the rest is the change. The lazy chart chunk is byte-identical across the pair at 197,960 B gzipped (584,860 B raw) under the same file hash, because no new chart type was registered - eleven engine-backed sparklines would have been eleven chart instances, and these are hand-written SVG. The prerendered console document moved 174,305 -> 175,542 gzipped bytes against a ceiling of 301,580, leaving 126,038 spare.
